fact: The East African Communications Organisation report lists Kenya, through its regulator CA, as one of the seven member states whose regulators submit data to EACO; no event date is given, so the report's published date is used.

EACO publishes Kenya's One Network Area cross-border voice figures for 2025: inbound 461.5 million minutes (+19.2%) and outbound 603.5 million minutes (+23.9%, the largest in the region), with roaming tariffs reduced under the ONA Project.

Kenya is named with Uganda, Rwanda and South Sudan as a partner state in the Northern Corridor Integration Projects, whose implementation clusters meeting in Kampala discussed a single digital market, roaming costs and a joint communications satellite study; the report is dated 2026-08-24 and gives no date for the meeting.

Uganda, Kenya, Rwanda and South Sudan opened a joint account at Standard Chartered Bank Uganda to receive partner-state contributions for a satellite feasibility study agreed under a roadmap settled at an April 2026 Nairobi meeting; the source dates the account only to its report of 2026-08-24, and says the study has not yet started pending deposits.

Kenya's Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy is named with the ministries of Nigeria, Togo, Namibia and Benin as announcing ATLAS Umoja AI, a pan-African initiative on African-language AI, on 2026-07-24 alongside the ATU Conference of Plenipotentiaries in Abuja; no agreement signing is stated.

The document states, citing Biometric Update, that the AfCFTA Secretariat's ADAPT cross-border data-exchange system announced a pilot with Kenya, Morocco and Nigeria in May 2026; no signed agreement is stated.
